subject: Expansion pricing and co-term for BrightScale
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan@brightscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightscale.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Expansion: mid-contract uplift + co-term question

Hi Marissa,

Quick question — we’re ramping faster than expected and want to add an additional committed capacity block (roughly an extra 200k generated tokens/month equivalent) starting Dec 1. Our current contract runs through Jan 31, 2026. Do you support a mid-contract uplift with co-terming (so everything ends on Jan 31), and will that be prorated?

Also, if we commit to the uplift now, is there any expansion discount or pricing band we should expect (we’re trying to forecast costs for Q1). If there are multiple options (prorated add-on vs. flat amendment for the remainder of the term), can you outline the economics?

cc’ing Dana (procurement) to loop in legal/PO questions.

Thanks,
Jordan

--
Jordan Park
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightScale
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@brightscale.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightscale.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Expansion: mid-contract uplift + co-term question

Hi Jordan — great to hear the ramp is ahead of plan. Short answers: yes, we support mid-contract uplifts and we can co-term to your existing Jan 31, 2026 end date (or another date if you prefer). We typically handle this two ways: 1) prorated add-on for the remainder of the term (simpler invoicing), or 2) an amendment that converts the uplift into a permanent committed increase and re-rates the entire contract for the co-term period.

What I recommend given your timing:
- Add-on (Dec 1–Jan 31): prorated charge for two months at the list uplift rate.
- If you want the uplift to persist beyond Jan 31, do the amendment now and co-term to Jan 31 so the new committed quantity and discounted band apply immediately on Dec 1 and carry through the co-term.

Discount guidance (high level):
- <250k tokens/month uplift: standard uplift pricing, no change to tier.
- 250k–750k uplift: 7.5% volume discount on the incremental block if converted to a committed amendment.
- >750k uplift: tiered discounting and custom pricing (requires finance approval).

I’ve attached a quick pricing workbook and an amendment template to show the math and example language. If you can confirm which option you prefer (prorate-only vs. full amendment/co-term) and whether legal should review the amendment now, I’ll pull in Marcus to lock the discount band.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred approach and target co-term date.
2) If amendment, who is your legal contact for execution?
3) We’ll produce an amendment + DocuSign and share PO/invoicing guidance.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: redwood_uplift_pricing_v1.xlsx, amendment_template.docx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Park <jordan@brightscale.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Expansion: mid-contract uplift + co-term question

Hi all — copying the pricing guidance so it’s on record. For a mid-contract uplift that converts to a committed quantity through the co-term we recommend: 

Option A (prorated add-on):
- Dec 1–Jan 31: prorated usage charge at list uplift rate (no discount), invoiced on the regular subscription invoice.

Option B (amendment + co-term to Jan 31):
- If BrightScale signs an amendment that increases committed tokens by >=250k/month, we can apply a 7.5% discount on the incremental committed price for the co-term period. 
- We can also offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied to the first invoice after amendment) up to $7,500 for migration/engineering effort.
- Billing: amendment effective Dec 1, invoices prorated for the first partial month, then normal monthly billing thereafter.

Notes: any requests to change the co-term to a non-calendar fiscal cutover (e.g., Mar 31) are doable but will require re-calculation of PRORATE and potential change to the discount cadence. If they want to co-term to Mar 31 instead of Jan 31, we need to know whether the uplift is temporary (two months) or permanent.

Happy to approve the 7.5% band for this deal provided we get the signed amendment and an explicit uplift quantity.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Jordan Park <jordan@brightscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightscale.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 08:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Expansion: mid-contract uplift + co-term question

Thanks Marissa and Marcus — this is helpful. Couple follow-ups from procurement/finance: 
1) Can we shift the co-term to Mar 31, 2026 (aligns with our fiscal year close)? We’d prefer the new committed quantity to run through Mar 31 rather than Jan 31.
2) For the 7.5% incremental discount: will that apply retroactively to Dec 1 invoice if we sign the amendment now (i.e., cover Dec and Jan), or only after the amendment is executed?
3) We also have a one-time migration cost (engineering hours to integrate the additional capacity). Would Redwood consider a one-time credit against the first invoice (or a portion of it)?

We’re leaning toward a permanent amendment (Option B) but need clarification on the above to finalize with legal and finance. Dana is on the thread for the PO and legal routing.

—Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@brightscale.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@brightscale.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Expansion: mid-contract uplift + co-term question

Jordan — thanks, and happy we’re close. Responses inline: 
1) Co-term to Mar 31, 2026 — we can do this. Because it extends the co-term window we’ll re-calc the effective committed period; the incremental discount (7.5%) still applies for the co-term period so long as the uplift quantity is >=250k/month. Marcus, confirming we’re OK to apply the 7.5% across Dec–Mar if amendment is signed.
2) Retroactivity — yes, if the amendment is fully executed and the effective date on the amendment is Dec 1, 2025, we will apply the discount retroactively to Dec 1 and adjust the Dec invoice accordingly. That requires signature on the amendment before the Dec invoice closes.
3) One-time credit — we can provide a one-time onboarding credit of $7,500 applied to the first post-amendment invoice.

Next steps: I attached a prepared amendment (amendment_for_signature.pdf) with Dec 1 effective date and co-term to Mar 31, 2026, and the pricing schedule filled based on the uplift quantities you mentioned. Can you review and confirm legal contact for signature? I’ve also created a DocuSign envelope — link below — to speed this along. Once signed we’ll issue an adjusted invoice and confirm PO requirements.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If you’re comfortable, let’s target signature by Nov 30 so billing can reflect the change for Dec 1. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk legal through the amendment if helpful.

Best,
